verdict.reasoning: Patient says the headache has been going on for a few days and started “around three days ago, maybe.”
Patient states, “it kind of feels all over my head, but like mainly around my right eye.”

Patient describes it as “kind of… dull, but sometimes it gets a bit sharper” and that it became worse over days: “by the end of the day it was… a lot… then I woke up the next morning like it was even, even worse… You think the headache is getting worse…? Patient: “Yeah.”
Patient reports light sensitivity: “light is quite annoying my eyes.” When asked if it hurts to look at bright lights, patient answers, “Yeah, yeah, it hurts.”
On nausea/vomiting: Patient says, “basically I'm sick with the headache, but I. No vomiting.” This indicates nausea without vomiting.
Doctor asks, “Any recent head injuries at all?” Patient: “No.”
Patient says previous similar headaches improved with ibuprofen: “in the past did help me… but this time it's just not.”
When asked about migraine history, patient states, “Not myself. I've never had a migraine, but my sister and my mum have them quite frequently.”
Doctor asks, “do you take any regular medication?” Patient replies, “No.”
Patient says, “So I tried ibuprofen… I took like a few for the last two days… How many tablets…? Three a day.” She reports no relief: “But it doesn't really help.”

Doctor notes underdosing: “You can take up to two tablets three times a day,” but does not explicitly state a plan to increase her ibuprofen dose to the maximum; it is presented as an option, not a defined plan.
Doctor says, “Or I can prescribe you something stronger like naproxen, which is another anti inflammatory, which can be helpful.” This states a plan to prescribe naproxen as an alternative.
Doctor: “We can also add in other painkillers like paracetamol or codeine… I can give you a prescription for that today.” This supports considering and prescribing codeine if required.
Doctor asks, “Do you have any allergies to any medications?” Patient: “Not that I know of.”
Patient: “my sister and my mum have [migraines] quite frequently.”
Patient says, “I work in it, so I work with computers a lot, so it kind of is difficult to focus. I had to like reduce the brightness of my screen,” indicating IT work with screen-related eye strain.

On smoking/alcohol: Patient: “I socially smoke and I drink. Not only socially.” Doctor summarizes, “Only socially.” Although there is slight nuance about alcohol, the statement that she smokes and drinks socially is consistent.
Doctor states assessment: “I do think this could be a headache very similar to migraine… I think it's something for us to think about.”
Doctor links family history: “given your mum and your sister also have migraines. I think it's something for us to think about,” implying a possible genetic component.

Transcript does not explicitly list photophobia, nausea, and ineffective ibuprofen as the reasons for the suspected diagnosis; only family history and suggestive history are mentioned, so attributing those specific features as considered suggestive is an inferred rationale not stated.
Doctor advises, “it may be worth keeping a headache diary so we can try and work out what's… If there's any triggers which could be causing your headaches to become worse.”

Doctor: “I'd like you to come back and see me in about a week's time. Week to two weeks time… In the meantime, if your headaches aren't getting any better or they're getting worse… give me a call or come back and see me sooner.”

Doctor asks about vision and speech: “Any problems? Your eyesight or your vision?” Patient denies loss of vision: “Not loss of vision, I wouldn't say.” Later, “Any difficulty with speaking or speech? Patient: “No.”
Doctor: “Any difficulty with weakness in your arms and legs?” Patient: “No.”
Doctor: “Any neck pain or neck stiffness?” Patient: “No.”
Doctor asks, “Any temperatures or fevers?” Patient: “No.” Then, “Any rashes at all on your skin?” Patient: “No, none of that I've noticed.”

Systems review includes vision and speech: patient reports “Not loss of vision” and, to “Any difficulty with speaking or speech?” answers “No,” making ROS negative for loss of vision or speech difficulty.
ROS for neurological symptoms: To “Any difficulty with weakness in your arms and legs?” patient answers “No,” so negative for weakness.
ROS for neck symptoms: “Any neck pain or neck stiffness?” Patient: “No,” thus negative.
ROS for constitutional/skin: patient denies “temperatures or fevers” and “rashes,” making it negative for fever or rash.
